description.Name: EEG Data for Emotion Recognition: Alcohol Cue-Reactivity Dataset (Alcohol Dependence vs Healthy Controls)

latestSnapshot.readme:
Alcohol cue-reactivity EEG: alcohol use disorder vs control (Neuphony FlexCap)

OVERVIEW
This dataset contains EEG recorded while participants watched alcohol-related and neutral audiovisual
stimuli. The main purpose of the dataset is the recognition of emotion from EEG: a happy alcoholic
video (positive emotion) and a sad alcoholic video (negative emotion) were included to evoke different
emotional states. The study compares Alcohol_Dependent participants (alcohol use disorder, AUD) with Healthy_Control participants.

PARTICIPANTS
60 participants: 30 Alcohol_Dependent (patients with AUD, recruited from the Kanoria Rehabilitation Center) and 30 Healthy_Control.
All participants are male.
Each participant completed up to 3 trials (180 recordings in total).
Participant labels: sub-01 to sub-30 are Alcohol_Dependent (original codes P1-P30); sub-31 to sub-60 are Healthy_Control (original codes C1-C30).
Each trial is stored as one BIDS session: ses-01 = trial 1, ses-02 = trial 2, ses-03 = trial 3.
The group of each participant is in participants.tsv.

DATA FORMAT AND PROCESSING
- The EEG data are provided as EDF files in BIDS format (sub-*/ses-*/eeg/*_eeg.edf), one file per trial (session).
- The data were only trimmed and labelled according to the video stimulus cues. Each recording was
  trimmed to the 116 s stimulus sequence (starting at the start of the video), and the stimulus segments
  were labelled in the events files (segment onsets = video start timestamp plus fixed offsets).
- No other processing was applied: no filtering, re-referencing or artifact removal.
- Unit: microvolts (uV). The exported CSV files contain raw, unfiltered EEG in uV
  (confirmed by Neuphony support).

EEG RECORDING
- Device: Neuphony FlexCap, 8-channel EEG, dry electrodes, portable
- Channels: Fp1, Fp2, F3, F4, O1, O2, Fz, Pz (10-20 system)
- Reference: A1/A2
- Sampling rate: 250 Hz
- Mains frequency: 50 Hz
- Electrode positions were not digitized; the channel names follow the standard 10-20 system.

TASK AND STIMULI (task-cuereactivity)
One trial lasts 116 s (29,000 samples). Segments (see *_events.tsv for the exact onsets and durations):
  - baseline: Relaxing nature video at the start of the trial (baseline relaxation)
  - alcohol_bottle_image: Alcohol bottle image (alcoholic cue)
  - Relaxation: Relaxing music with a white screen (relaxation period between cues)
  - happy_alcoholic_video: Happy alcoholic video (positive alcohol association)
  - sad_alcoholic_video: Sad alcoholic video (negative alcohol association)
  - control_beverage_video: Non-alcoholic beverages video (control cue)

FILES
- sub-*/ses-*/eeg/*_eeg.edf: EEG data (EDF), one file per trial (ses-01 to ses-03)
- sub-*/ses-*/eeg/*_eeg.json: recording information (device, task, reference, sampling rate)
- task-cuereactivity_channels.tsv: channel information (the same 8 channels for every recording)
- sub-*/ses-*/eeg/*_events.tsv: stimulus segments (trial_type, onset, duration)
- task-cuereactivity_events.json: description of the event columns (applies to all sessions)
- participants.tsv / participants.json: group

ETHICS
Approved by the Nirma University ethics committee
Consent was obtained from all participants.

CONTACT

metadata.studyDesign: Case-control EEG study comparing Alcohol_Dependent (n=30) and Healthy_Control (n=30) male participants. Each participant completed 3 trials of a 116 s audiovisual sequence: baseline relaxation video, alcohol bottle image, happy alcoholic video, sad alcoholic video and a non-alcoholic beverage video, separated by relaxation blocks. EEG was recorded with an 8-channel Neuphony FlexCap (dry electrodes, 250 Hz).
